subject: Dedicated capacity options & activation roadmap for Sundance AI
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@sundanceai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@sundanceai.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: Dedicated capacity options for Sundance AI

Hi Karthik,

We’re evaluating dedicated inference capacity for our production LLM endpoints and want a concise set of reservation options so our leadership and procurement can compare economics and risk. Key constraints: P95 latency target ~150ms for 8k context, predictable monthly cost, and the ability to scale quickly during product launches.

Specific asks:
- Example cluster sizes tied to expected throughput buckets (small/medium/large)
- Minimum guaranteed GPU commitment and how that impacts price
- Suggested ramp schedule over the first 6 months with warm-up credits or pre-warm options
- Any flexibility for burst or regional failover during the first 90 days

Could you send a short proposal or template we can review this week? I’ve attached our RFP for context.

Thanks —
Samira Khan
Head of Platform, Sundance AI
samira.k@sundanceai.com

Attachments: Sundance_RFP_2026.pdf (PDF, RFP, 3 pages)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@sundanceai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_b@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, procurement@sundanceai.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Dedicated capacity options for Sundance AI

Hi Samira — great to connect. Thanks for sharing the RFP. I attached a one-page outline that maps three practical reservation bands to expected throughput and cost. High level summary below, and I’m happy to walk through numbers on a call.

Attachments: Sundance_Dedicated_Proposal_v1.pdf (PDF, 2 pages); Sundance_MAPlist.xlsx (XLSX, token/throughput assumptions)

Proposal highlights (summary):
- Band A (Onramp): 8 GPU reserved minimum (NVIDIA A10s equivalent), supports ~150 rps of short-text generation with continuous batching; recommended for pilots & prod baseline. Estimated activation + warmup credits for first 30 days.
- Band B (Growth): 32 GPU reserve with burst pool up to 48 GPUs. Targets medium production use (early scale, 1M tokens/day). Staged ramp: 8 -> 16 (month 1) -> 24 (month 3) -> 32 (month 4).
- Band C (Scale): 96 GPU reserved footprint with automatic burst and regional mirroring for availability. Suggested for customers expecting sustained high throughput or multi-region workloads. Typical ramp: 32 -> 64 (month 2) -> 96 (month 4).

Minimum guaranteed GPU and price impact:
- We publish committed discounts by reservation band. The per-token and per-hour economics improve at 32 GPUs and above due to fixed overhead amortization and batch window adjustments. If you lock a 12-month commit starting at 32 GPUs, we can offer a stepped discount schedule.

Warm-up and activation:
- 30-day warmup credits (partial) + one-time pre-warm allocation to populate KV caches and reduce initial p95 tail. We recommend a 2-week canary with smaller lane reserved to validate perf before full traffic shift.

Bursting & failover:
- Cross-region fallback and soft-burst of non-reserved capacity available for critical launches (subject to capacity). We’ll document SLA/credits in proposal.

Next steps:
- If useful, I’ll route a technical appendix from Ben (runtime) that maps GPU SKUs to latency/throughput for 8k and 32k contexts. Can we schedule a 30-min call on Wed or Thu to align on numbers and MAP (mutual action plan)?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_b@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Sundance capacity notes (technical appendix draft)

Karthik / Lauren —

Quick technical notes to include in the appendix for Samira:
- GPU SKU guidance: for Sundance’s latency target at 8k, recommend NV A100 40GB or equivalent 80GB Q8 path if you need 32k context. If they want cost-optimized paths, we can propose quantized 4-bit variants (Q4_0) that save ~30% GPU-hours but may impact small-sample quality for certain prompts.
- Minimum activation: 8 GPUs is fine for functional baseline, but for predictable p95 at peak bursts, recommend baseline 16 GPUs with autoscale headroom. This avoids SLO misses during burst windows.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for any steady-state calls (saves ~18-25% token compute). Include a note about cache warmers and priming tokens for the first 48 hours.
- Warmup credits: suggest 1000 pre-warmed queries equivalent (we give tokens credit) and a 14-day SLA-exempt warm-up window to avoid billing surprises.

I’ll produce a short table mapping estimated p95 vs GPU count and typical batch sizes.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Hi Karthik,

Thank you for the outline. A few clarifications so our procurement and finance teams can model cost and risk:
1) Can you provide the per-GPU-hour rate for each band (A/B/C) and the committed discount schedule for 12/24 month terms?
2) What is the explicit minimum GPU guarantee (contractual) for Band A and Band B?
3) How are warmup credits issued and applied on invoices?
4) Is there an SLA credit policy if p95 exceeds target for more than X hours in a billing month?
5) Who will be the technical onboarding owner and what is a typical onboarding timeline (we need to coordinate security/compliance review)?

We attached a short template with our procurement fields. Please respond by EOD Monday so we can finalize internal approvals.

Regards,

Sundance AI

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Sundance RFP: clarifications on reservation economics and SLA

Hi —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Answers and a proposed mutual action plan below. I’ve also attached the same two-doc packet we referenced earlier.

Answers (concise):
1) Per-GPU-hour (list price, pre-discount): Band A (8 GPUs): $3.20 / GPU-hour; Band B (32 GPUs): $2.75 / GPU-hour; Band C (96 GPUs): $2.30 / GPU-hour. Committed discounts: 12-month: 10% at 32+ GPUs; 24-month: 15% at 32+ GPUs. Precise pricing will be in the final SOW.
2) Minimum GPU guarantee: Band A messages in proposal set the contractual minimum at 8 GPUs. For predictable SLOs we recommend starting at 16 GPUs operationally; contractually we can structure a 90-day ramp clause (8 -> 16 -> 32) with predefined milestones.
3) Warmup credits: issued as an invoice credit line item, consumed against first 2 months of invoicing. We typically grant a lump-sum token credit (example: equivalent of 1,000,000 tokens) and show it as "Warmup credit - Sundance AI" on month 1/2 invoices.
4) SLA credits: we publish an SLA table in the SOW. Example: if p95 latency target exceeded cumulatively for >8 hours in billing month, we provide pro-rated service credit; for sustained >72 hours we offer additional remediation (technical prioritization + credit). Exact language to be included in SOW.
5) Onboarding owner & timeline: Ben Carter will lead technical onboarding (security/compliance touchpoints with your SecOps). Typical timeline: 2 weeks security review (concurrent), 2 weeks canary + priming (validation), then progressive ramp over 8 weeks. Total from contract signature to full-ramp ~10–12 weeks.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
- Week 0 (Contract signature): Issue initial invoice with warmup credits applied and schedule onboarding kickoff.
- Weeks 1–2: Security & compliance review, credentialing, environment provisioning.
- Weeks 3–4: Canary lane active (8->16 GPUs), KV cache warmup, test load.
- Weeks 5–8: Progressive ramp to target band (32 GPUs or agreed band).
- Week 12: Full traffic shift, monitoring & post-mortem.

Next steps: I’ll drop a calendar invite for a 30-min alignment with Samira, your procurement lead, Ben and Lauren to sign off on the MAP and the pricing table. If procurement needs a redlineable SOW, we can have a draft to you within 48 hours.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
